analysis:
The only change in this batch is to docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the date bump at line 3 and a new paragraph at head lines 334-343 about SIGHUP. It states that SIGHUP now enters the graceful drain for hand-started providers (`start --local`, or `start --foreground` run in a terminal), so that closing the terminal drains instead of killing the process. It also says SIGHUP is not a stop signal for the launchd job or when SIGHUP was ignored at start (nohup), and that a self-update re-exec carries the same choice into the new process. The behavior is attributed to `ProviderStopSignals` in `provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Service/ProviderStopSignals.swift`. That code was not supplied, so the described behavior is unverified.

Security relevance: this is documentation only, and no security controls, endpoints or trust boundaries change. If the described code is real, SIGHUP-triggered drain is a local-process lifecycle signal. It is relevant at most to T-010 (drain and cancellation availability) and TB-003 (local operator). A local operator can already stop the provider, so it adds no privilege or data exposure. A drain preserves accepted-work completion, which is a mild availability improvement.

Open question for later passes: the SIGHUP handling and re-exec inheritance in ProviderStopSignals.swift. No finding is raised. The documentation makes no security claim that could be invalidated.
